one_liner: Small Java HTTP server and web framework on a JNI epoll core; ties C++ cinatra and lithium in TechEmpower plaintext.
what_it_does: wizzardo-http, a one-person project now renamed wizzardo/webery, is a Java 8+ HTTP/1.1 server with a small web framework on top. It offers lambda handlers (new HttpServer<>(8080).getUrlMapping().append(path, (req, resp) -> ...)) and controllers with URL mapping and path variables. The framework adds dependency injection, a Groovy Config.groovy with environments and profiles, a GSP-style template engine, i18n, static files, sessions, multipart, websockets and SSL. It is its own API, not a Servlet container, so it is not a drop-in for anything.
how_it_is_fast: On Linux, I/O runs through the author's wizzardo/epoll library. Its C core (EpollCore.c, gcc -Ofast, called over JNI) does accept4 with SOCK_NONBLOCK and TCP_NODELAY, edge-triggered epoll_wait, and read/write straight from direct ByteBuffers by raw address. Responses are assembled from preallocated direct buffers: cached status lines, 'Content-Length: N' for N < 1024, header constants, and a Date header re-rendered once per second. They are copied with native memcpy helpers (copyInto2 to copyInto5). Request parsing interns method, version and known header strings through a byte trie (ByteTree), so a hit allocates no String, and finds line ends with a stride-2 CR/LF scan. Pipelined requests from one read are handled in a loop and flushed once. In the TechEmpower setup, handlers run directly on one I/O thread per core, with no worker pool.
when_to_use: Small self-contained JSON or plaintext microservices on Linux x86-64 or aarch64, where you want a single fat jar with routing, DI and templates and few dependencies.
High request rates of tiny keep-alive or pipelined HTTP/1.1 responses served from I/O threads, the shape the TechEmpower plaintext and JSON tests measure.
Experimenting with JNI-based socket I/O in Java as an alternative to Netty's native epoll transport.
when_not_to_use: Anything that needs a maintained ecosystem. It has one maintainer and 221 stars, the last Maven Central release (com.wizzardo:http 0.4) dates from 2020-08-28, master is 0.5-SNAPSHOT, and TechEmpower marked the test 'broken' on 2026-02-10 (PR #10708: 'Fail in the last runs').

macOS or Windows: off Linux it falls back to Java NIO, which the maintainer says 'might be not optimised at all'. In issue #10 it served 58,623 req/s against 616,765 for robaho's httpserver on the same Mac.
As evidence that Java beats C++: the TechEmpower result is a tie at the top-of-table cluster (cinatra 0.04% ahead, lithium 0.02% behind), and the socket hot path is C reached over JNI.
Copying the TechEmpower configuration (onlyCachedHeaders = true with a trimmed string cache) into production: request headers are then dropped, see gotchas.
Blocking handlers with workersCount 0 (the TechEmpower setting): handlers run on the I/O threads, so a slow handler stalls every connection on that thread.

integration.form: Maven/Gradle jar (com.wizzardo:http 0.4 on Maven Central) plus a per-platform JNI native library from com.wizzardo:epoll
integration.dependencies: com.wizzardo:epoll (native libepoll-core .so for x32, x64 and aarch64 Linux; libepoll-ssl needs OpenSSL), com.wizzardo.tools:tools, com.wizzardo:simple-websocket-client. Master pins epoll 0.3.5-SNAPSHOT and tools 0.24-SNAPSHOT from the OSSRH snapshots repository; 0.4 pins epoll 0.3.4 and tools 0.23
integration.min_toolchain: Java 8 (source/target 1.8; CI on JDK 8). Built with Gradle 6.8, whose 'compile' configuration no longer exists in Gradle 7+. The TechEmpower image used openjdk 11.0.3.
integration.platforms: Linux (x86, x86-64, aarch64) through native epoll; other OSes and EPOLL_DISABLED=true use the slow Java NIO fallback
integration.thread_safety: Handlers can run concurrently on several I/O threads or a worker pool (ioWorkersCount, workersCount). Controllers are prototype-scoped and services singletons in the DI container. Thread safety of shared application state is otherwise not documented.

gotchas: Benchmark-only parsing shortcut (harness flaw). The TechEmpower app overrides initHttpPartsCache() to seed the string cache with only the HTTP method names and 'HTTP/1.1', and Config.groovy sets onlyCachedHeaders = true. In HttpHeadersReader.getValue every string missing from that cache comes back null, so no request header is ever stored: Host, Connection: close and Content-Length are all ignored. Reading the current source, an HTTP/1.0 request leaves protocol null and hits a NullPointerException in prepareKeepAlive, which becomes a 400 and a closed connection. The library default is onlyCachedHeaders = false, yet the entry is classified 'Realistic'.

The TechEmpower config sets the server name to 'W', so responses carry 'Server: W' instead of the default 'Server: wizzardo', 7 bytes less on every response. TechEmpower's rules expect the Server header to be 'whatever is normal for the platform or framework'. Fewer bytes per response may matter in a plaintext table whose top 18 entries sit within 1.9% of each other (derived from the screenshot).

The measured build is the 2020 0.4 release on JDK 11.0.3 with -XX:+UseParallelGC and the deprecated -XX:+AggressiveOpts, not the current master. The test no longer builds or runs in TechEmpower, so the result cannot be reproduced from TFB master.
The I/O core is native C code (gcc -Ofast) that handles raw buffer addresses passed from Java as jlong. A bad offset or length is a native memory fault, not a Java exception.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Among the Java siblings, Netty, Undertow and Vert.x are far more mature, and firenio placed above wizzardo-http in the same Round 22 plaintext table (rank 5, 7,004,779 vs 6,995,129). Pick wizzardo-http only if you want a tiny all-in-one Linux framework (routing, DI, templates) in one jar and can live with a single maintainer; for production Java HTTP, prefer Vert.x or Netty.
verified_claims_summary: TechEmpower Round 22 plaintext (Dell R440 Xeon Gold 5120, 10 GbE, pipelined 'Hello, World!' at up to 16,384 connections), read from a third-party screenshot. wizzardo-http, as com.wizzardo:http 0.4 on openjdk 11.0.3, ranked 8th of 486 at 6,995,129 responses/s, between C++ cinatra (6,998,076) and C++ lithium (6,993,976), and 0.3% above C libreactor (6,971,119, derived). That is a tie inside a saturated top cluster, measured with a benchmark-specific configuration that skips request-header storage and shortens the Server header.
status_note: Stale (last commit 2025-05-11; the TechEmpower entry has been marked broken since 2026-02-10) but MIT-licensed. The last release is 0.4 from 2020, master depends on SNAPSHOT artifacts from the retired OSSRH snapshot repository, and the Linux speed depends on the author's JNI epoll native library, so treat it as a reference design rather than something to adopt.
